The native evaluator creates round-specific scratch/input files and launches each selected candidate; it does not reuse candidate scores. DevicePoolCache applies only to training gathers, not native admission or GP scoring. Source-array replacement on promotion invalidates the cache; promotion185→round186 and186→187 each report one transfer. All187–205 native results finished, with no timeouts. Parent offsets varied and proposed operator types included all six observed categories.

Rounds200/201: total103.09/96.43s, GP100.56/91.11s, training2.17/4.57s. Same-context/same-DSL timing comparisons (20/23 matches) give median wall ratios1.6116/1.7265 against the other audited rounds. Round201 slate assembly rose.67→2.45s, device packing.055→.279s, while model/targets rose only.54→.62s. This is consistent with temporary shared-host CPU/scheduling contention, not a returning multi-GB packing leak. There are no historical host samples to identify a particular consumer. Timings recovered subsequently.

Policy defect: the existing GP exploration trigger used only adapter-rejection streaks. Accepted dev ties reset it despite a long GP promotion drought. A reproducing test fails on the old source. Correct the GP trigger independently of adapter admission:18 consecutive completed zero-promotion rounds trigger three exploration rounds, then three ranked-only cooldown rounds; promotion or missing/unknown/evaluation-free history resets the drought count. Exploration reuses16 generated proposals and two ranked plus two seeded random choices; max4 evaluated/context,64/round. No LR/step/dev/DOPE/evaluator/gate change and no quality-gain promise. Preregistration is written before the checkpoint-boundary installation.
